title: Sonny and the Dewdrop World | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka discovers that every single dewdrop on the grass holds a perfect tiny world inside it — a curved reflection of the whole bush, complete with tiny trees and a tiny upside-down moon. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The grass was full of worlds.

Sunny was lying very still, nose almost to the ground, looking at the dew that had settled in the night. Each dewdrop was a sphere — perfect, round, trembling slightly when the breeze moved through — and inside each one was a whole scene.

She looked into the nearest one.

Inside: a curved, miniature bush. Tiny trees, tiny sky, the moon upside-down and small. A perfect reflection of the world above, bent by the curve of the water into something smaller and rounder. The grass blades on the other side of the drop looked enormous. Her own enormous eye was visible in the very centre.

She looked into the next one.

Almost the same. Almost — but the angle was slightly different, so the trees were in a different place, the moon at a different height. Each drop held its own version of the world.

She sat up and looked across the whole meadow.

Millions of them. Every blade of grass heavy with tiny worlds.

She thought: the world is being held so many times over. Every drop of dew is looking after a piece of it.

She lay back down with her cheek against the cool grass.

The drops trembled gently around her.

Miniature moons in every direction.

All of them watching her sleep.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, dewdrop world. Goodnight, little one.
